sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Trier has raised street and permit prices and closed streets in its centre. From 1 January 2024 street parking inside the Alleenring costs €2.80 an hour, up from €2.20, and €1.40 in the outer zone, with app payment about 10 cents cheaper until the end of 2025 [1][3]. The proposal had been €3.00 and €1.50, put forward in September 2023 [0]. The resident permit rose from the national €30.70 to €200 a year, with the zone South extended southwards to Aulstraße. The administration originally planned steps up to €365 by 2028, and set the fees without a council vote under a new state rule that only requires councils to be 'heard' [2]. In December 2024 the council voted 38 to 13 to freeze the fee at €200, rather than add €40 a year [7].

The city's parking concept says its aims are less parking-search traffic and moving long stays into garages, with garage tariffs always lower than on-street or large open car parks. From January 2024 that means €2.80 an hour on the street and €2.40 in the garages [4]. The centre has also become harder to drive into. Under the Urban Security Concept the pedestrian zone has been extended around the Domfreihof, Konstantinstraße and Neustraße, with parking spaces removed. The Stockplatz bollards were in operation from 24 June 2026, completing five bollard lines around the Hauptmarkt, and vehicles need an exemption permit [16]. In May 2024 the Freie Wähler said, citing the administration, that 82 of the 162 spaces in the affected area had been removed without replacement, amid criticism from the chamber of commerce and the CDU [5]. In August 2025 the CDU, Greens and FDP coalition proposed cheaper garage tariffs on low-demand weekdays and at night, which were proposals at that date [12].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main change is pricing in the Stadtwerke Trier (SWT) garages. From 1 January 2026 SWT cut the hourly price for its digital 'Komfort-Parken' (app plus licence-plate recognition) from €2.40 to €1.92 in five garages, with the scheme running initially for one year [13]. From 1 April 2026 it added a night offer of €15 a month for parking from 17:00 to 09:00 [14]. In May 2026 the Plaza-Carrée garage was fitted with new machines, barriers and plate recognition, and its tariff was cut to €1.20 per 30 minutes, with a €18 daily maximum, and both schemes now work there too [15].

The city says the seven garages it lists have a capacity of about 3,200 spaces that are only very rarely fully occupied [4]. Ostallee, the garage by the station, has 860 spaces at €2.40 an hour and €18 a day, according to Deutsche Bahn's listing [18]. Passenger trains returned to Trier's West Line on 3 March 2025, and the city describes park-and-ride sites with 30 spaces at Hafenstraße and 40 at Euren as planned [9]. It designates two free park-and-ride sites, at Messepark and Trier-Nord [19]. A city report counts 8,880 out-commuters to Luxembourg, and out-commuting has risen 24.4% since 2015 [10]. We found no sourced figures on a shift to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Stadtwerke Trier, through SWT Parken GmbH, runs the seven public garages and underground car parks the city lists around the centre, which are open around the clock, with a guidance system showing free capacity [17]. Our measured data cover seven car parks with 3,003 spaces from the SWT feed, with abbreviated names (such as Basi, Hauptm, Osta) that we have not matched to the city's list. We have no usable position data for them, so we say nothing about distances.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 39% on weekdays and 23% at weekends. The fullest is Basi (62% on weekdays, only 18% at weekends, 436 spaces), followed by ParkPlaza (44%), City and Kons (both 41%), Bahnhof (37%) and Hauptm (32%). The 715-space Osta is the emptiest at 26%. Over 2022 to 2025 the five garages with full histories (City, Hauptm, Kons, Basi, Osta) fell from 39% to 36%, with Kons rising from 31% to 39% and Hauptm falling from 38% to 29%. ParkPlaza rose from 32% in 2022 to 46% in 2025. The data cover the summer holidays and the university break, so term-time figures may differ.
